      "blurb": "Ramen by Ra, which opened in December, is a small counter in the glass-enclosed Bowery Market on the Lower East Side.     {
      "title": "The Best NYC Restaurants For Dining Solo",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/great-restaurants-for-dining-solo",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Ramen By Ra specializes in asa-style ramen, or breakfast ramen. Bowls are loaded with things like bacon, egg, and cheese, or steak and egg, or tomato-egg drop, all of which are delightful with a cup of hojicha by yourself. The restaurant is closet-sized and gets nice afternoon sun, so block off time on a weekday, and have lunch here."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Ramen In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-ramen-nyc",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "In the East Village, Ramen By Ra is the only spot on this list that specializes in asa-style, or breakfast ramen. Their BEC ramen comes with thick slabs of bacon, a perfectly gooey marinated egg, and a light snowfall of parmesan cheese, and it’s just one of the bowls at this extremely charming counter. All their ramen starts with a base of a clear shoyu broth, with flavorful oils added to each bowl, like chimichurri oil on the standout steak and egg ramen. They also offer cups of broth and breakfast bao at their walk-up window."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Restaurants In The East Village",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/the-best-restaurants-in-the-east-village",
      "position": 21,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "There are a lot of ramen shops in the East Village, but only one that specializes in asa-style, or breakfast ramen. The tiny spot on 1st Street serves bowls topped with bacon, egg, and cheese, or lox. It’s a bit of a pain to make a reservation, but we love their food—especially the steak and eggs with a very vibrant chimichurri, and they do sell cups of broth and bao from their front window."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Spots Of The Winter, NYC Edition ",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/spots-of-winter-ny",
      "position": 13,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Yes, winter is all about fire-lit nights, but it’s also all about soup for breakfast. Skip that bodega BEC, and instead get Ramen By Ra’s noodles with thick slabs of bacon, marinated eggs, and showers of parmesan cheese. The tiny, sun-soaked East Village spot, with cozy cabinets and sparkling crystal bowls, specializes in asa-style, or breakfast ramen, and it really hits the spot on a chilly day. You’ll have to book in advance—or you can stop by for some takeaway broth or a breakfast bao in the morning."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Toughest Reservations In NYC Right Now (And How To Get Them)",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/toughest-restaurant-reservations-nyc",
      "position": 8,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "**Verdict: **The East Village iteration of Ramen By Ra has 50% more seating than the now-closed Noho location. Unfortunately, that only adds up to a total of six seats. The place is understandably a pain to get into, but if you need something more stylish than your usual noodle soup, it’s worth keeping an eye on their reservation page. Start with the bao stuffed with lox and fluffy cream cheese, then try the steak-and-egg ramen with sliced ribeye and zippy chimichurri oil."
    }

      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/previously-impossible-reservations-you-can-get-now",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "**How far in advance should you book? **Three weeks.\n\nWhen Bong—another member of our [Top 25](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc)—opened in Crown Heights in 2025, you could only book a table via Instagram DM. Eventually, they started taking reservations online, but that somehow only made it more difficult to get in. This was frustrating, given the fact that their rotating Cambodian menu doesn’t miss. Now, the closet-sized place is finally more accessible, partly because they added bookable outdoor seating. Reserve three weeks ahead, and you should be able to eat at a time that isn’t weird."
    },
    {
      "title": "NYC’s Best New Dishes Of 2025",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-new-dishes-nyc-2025",
      "position": 11,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Bone-In Heritage Pork Chop\n\nAt one of our [top-rated restaurants](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc#bong), the lobster is the biggest ticket on a short, Cambodian menu, and the fried fish is most photogenic. But Bong’s bone-in pork chop managed to do the impossible, erasing all our past dry-pork-chop associations with just one juicy bite. Topped with blistered, almost stewed cherry tomatoes, its crisped-up fat and tender meat are doused in tuk trey ping poh. That a dish with so much fish saucy oomph comes out of such a tiny kitchen makes it all the more impressive."
    },
    {
      "title": "NYC’s Best New Restaurants Of 2025",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-new-restaurants-new-york-2025",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "#### **THE MOMENT WE KNEW WE LOVED IT **\n\nWhen we ate a juicy pork chop with burst cherry tomatoes below a painting of Bad Bunny in the buff.\n\n#### **A PERFECT ORDER FOR FOUR PEOPLE WHO PICK THE BONES CLEAN**\n\nThe whole menu. There are only around 12 dishes, but everything is worth it.\n\n#### **GO IF YOU LIKE…**\n\nTo party, with lobster. Places like [Mắm](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/mam) or [Cocina Consuelo](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/cocina-consuelo)."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Things We Ate In June 2025",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-dishes-infatuation-nyc-reviewers-ate-june-2025",
      "position": 11,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Golden Squid\n\nA close runner-up to the pork (and fried fish, and lobster...) at Bong. A coating of salted egg yolk makes the soft rings of lightly battered fried squid even softer. The golden sauce is a little grainy, like rubbing velvet the wrong way, and scallion oil adds another warm dimension."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Most Fun Dinner Spots In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/the-most-fun-dinner-spots-in-nyc",
      "position": 13,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "At this Cambodian restaurant in Crown Heights, the music is almost too loud and there's a painting of a partially nude Bad Bunny hung above the bathroom. Which is just to say, if your friends who throw the best parties finally opened that restaurant they always talk about after a few bottles of wine, it might look something like Bong. And the food, like fried squid slathered in salted egg yolk, or fatty pork chops covered in blistered tomatoes and fish sauce, also happens to be excellent."
    },
    {
      "title": "Top 25: The Best Restaurants In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc",
      "position": 12,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "If your friends who throw the best parties finally opened that restaurant they always talk about after a few bottles of wine, it might look something like Bong. At this tiny Cambodian spot in Crown Heights, Tierra Whack and A$AP Rocky bounce loudly off the lime-green walls, the fish mint comes from the chef’s aunt’s backyard, and your server might be a friend who’s just helping out for tonight. It might seem like the couple running this place is figuring things out as they go—but never when it comes to the seasonally changing food. For example, that fish mint comes on a crunchy, whole fried dorade that’s still mystifyingly tender inside. Fatty slivers of pork jowl tossed with chunks of melon soak up chili pickle dressing. Blistered tomatoes burst over a pork chop that couldn’t be dry if it tried. The little edge of chaos around you just feels like a final pinch of seasoning."
    }

      "position": 7,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "“Jody Williams is an old friend who my brother used to work with back when she was at Gusto, and Giorgione.       "title": "The Best Italian Restaurants In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-italian-restaurants-nyc",
      "position": 3,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "It's extremely hard to secure a reservation at Via Carota (one of [the best restaurants in NYC](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc)), and there's pretty much always a wait for walk-ins of two or more hours. A meal here should involve some of the dozen-plus vegetable dishes, the steak tartare-like svizzerina, and the cacio e pepe (which is non-optional)."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Italian Restaurants In The West Village",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-italian-restaurant-west-village",
      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Via Carota is mostly walk-in-only, and every single night you’ll find people lined up in the entryway, waiting for a table with a quiet desperation. Waits can be anywhere from one to three hours, and it confuses us emotionally to say that, yes, this place is worth a three-hour wait. The cacio e pepe is the best in the city, the garlicky chopped steak is richer and more compelling than the majority of non-chopped steaks, and sometimes you just feel like sitting in a dark room with taxidermy, rustic wooden cabinets, and the occasional actor who once starred alongside Scarlett Johansson."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Restaurants In The West Village",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/the-best-restaurants-in-the-west-village",
      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Via Carota is always busy, and there are several reasons why.     },
    {

      "blurb": "\"I literally just came back from there. I had a really good radicchio treviso salad with currants and pine nuts where the greens were kind of wilted.     {

      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Sometimes, we’re wrong. It’s rare, but it happens. Our initial review of Via Carota, for example, was pretty lukewarm. With its perfect mix of casual, buzzy atmosphere and impressive, unfussy food, this West Village restaurant has grown on us immensely over the years. It’s one of our favorite [Italian](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-italian-restaurants-nyc) spots in Manhattan, slightly edging out the latest iteration of sister restaurant [I Sodi](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/i-sodi), so swing by for some world-class cacio e pepe and a crisp, towering salad. Just be sure to arrive before 6pm. Via Carota is essentially walk-in only, with very limited reservations, and we aren’t the only ones who love this place."

      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "“I spend a lot of time in the West Village, and I love the people who do Via Carota and Buvette. I think they do a really great job. They’re always at the top of the list of restaurants to go to when I’m in town. There’s incredible Italian at Via Carota. You really can’t go wrong, just run down the menu, but you gotta get pasta, and they have a good wine selection.”"
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Eat At The Bar Right Now In NYC",
